First line

The first line of this paragraph is bold and blue, as set by the first-line pseudo-element. The rest of the paragraph keeps the normal weight and colour, however long it runs and wherever the line happens to break.

Three columns

Newspapers and magazines have set text in columns for centuries because short lines are easier to read. A browser balances the columns so that each holds about the same amount of text, moving lines between them until the last column is no longer than the first. Words in justified columns are spread so both edges line up, which leaves larger gaps when a line holds only a few long words. Hyphenation would help, but it is not used here, so the spacing is exactly what the browser computes from the words alone. This paragraph keeps going so that every column gets several lines of text to compare.

Two columns with a rule

Column rules are drawn in the middle of the gap between columns and run the full height of the column box.

Paragraph margins inside columns behave as they do anywhere else: they separate the paragraphs and collapse at the top of a column.

The last paragraph is short.
